This would be amazing if I could see it. I really hope the Moon is visible right now!

I'm in Alice Springs, Australia at 2026-11-10 18:27 ACST (UTC+0930) (2026-11-10T08:57:00Z in UTC), at latitude -23.698 degrees and longitude 133.8807 degrees. My astronomy app says the Sun's altitude is 5.086 degrees and its azimuth is 253.378 degrees, so it is above the horizon. It says the Moon's altitude is 16.793 degrees and its azimuth is 249.764 degrees, so it is above the horizon. The Moon is 1.32 percent illuminated, 13.169 degrees from the Sun, and 398861.4 kilometers away. The sky brightness is bright daylight, the sky is clear, and I'm an ordinary adult with normal unaided eyesight who knows roughly where to look.

Do you think I'd actually be able to spot it?

Probably not with unaided eyes—at least not reliably.

The Moon is technically above the horizon at altitude **16.8°**, but it is an extremely thin crescent: only **1.32% illuminated** and just **13.2° from the Sun**. With the Sun still **5.1° above the horizon**, the bright twilight/daylight sky will overwhelm the faint crescent. Its position—about **4° above and 3.6° east of the Sun** in azimuth—is also close to the bright solar glare, making it unsafe and difficult to search for.

If you try, wait until the Sun is fully below the horizon and use a clear, unobstructed western horizon, but **do not scan near the Sun with binoculars or a telescope**. Even after sunset, this very young crescent may remain challenging without optical aid. A camera with a telephoto lens, or binoculars used only once the Sun is safely below the horizon and nowhere near the field of view, would give you a much better chance.
